entrada.titulo: Enhancing anomaly detection and prevention in Internet of Things (IoT) using deep neural networks and blockchain based cyber security

perfil_anterior.problema: The author believes some security issues, such as data protection and model stability, are under-explored in the current study.
perfil_anterior.limites: Future research will focus on developing lightweight DNN architectures for IoT devices with limited resources
perfil_anterior.possibilidades: Integrar identidade auto‑soberana (SSI) para autenticação descentralizada dos dispositivos IoT em cidades inteligentes.; Aplicar criptografia baseada em atributos (ABE) para controle de acesso granular aos dados registrados no blockchain.; Explorar aprendizado federado combinado com DNNs‑BCT para melhorar a escalabilidade e privacidade em ambientes de edge computing.; Avaliar a abordagem em cenários de cidades inteligentes com múltiplas organizações públicas e privadas, medindo interoperabilidade e latência.

Abdullah Ayub Khan et al. 46 discussed the Secure Remote Sensing Data With BDLT. This paper processes 
an ideal data delivery mechanism for the smart cities analytical model using a secure blockchain distributed 
consortium network and Partial Swam Optimization (POS). There are three new parts to this piece of work. It 
provides a secure way to send data by integrating blockchain technology with machine learning to find the best 
way to send data across encrypted channels. NuCypher proxy re-encryption-enabled value encryption, a public 
key cryptographic method not using cipher conversion, is employed to carry out neighborhood encryption 
sequences. Thirdly, Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) can address smart cities’ data deliverance classification 
issues by improving record management and preservation.
Abdullah Ayub Khan et al. 47 deliberated the Blockchainlightweight Proof-of-Elapsed Time (B-LPoET) for 
efficient distributed transaction execution and security. To determine who has the authority to mine, participants 
may confirm their identities before joining, and the protocol can be enhanced from the default PoET to a 
lightweight version that can validate transactions and generate more blocks. By implementing a lightweight 
topology for winning node selection and waiting time utilizing multithreading, the B-LPoET architecture 
decreases the cost of multi-node efficiency and increases the system’s scalability. According to the experimental 
findings, the B-LPoET outperforms the current PoET and other state-of-the-art consensus algorithms. Table 2 
shows the comparison of existing methods.
Using DL models comprising autoencoders, DNNs, and AI-based systems connected with blockchain, the 
approaches find anomalies in IoMT and IoHT settings. Blockchain ensures data integrity and security; artificial 
intelligence models assist in identifying irregularities in realtime. Edge-based computing and multi-model 
feature extraction optimize system performance, providing practical answers for IoT network security and 
healthcare data protection.
Proposed method
Modern networks’ security needs a mix of sophisticated technology. This paper investigates blockchain-based 
threat response, DNN for network anomaly detection, and AI-powered anomaly detection combined with 
blockchain for IoT security. It also addresses DL models-based maritime and IoT traffic anomaly detection. 
These methodologies improve cybersecurity by guaranteeing data integrity, openness, and threat reduction.
Existing IoT anomaly detection techniques often suffer from elevated false alarm rates, ineffective real-time 
threat categorization, and susceptibility to adversarial attacks. Moreover, centralized security frameworks render 
IoT networks vulnerable to single points of failure, where corrupted nodes might threaten the integrity of the 
whole system. Current blockchain-based security models, while they guarantee data integrity, often experience 
significant computational overhead and delay, restricting their practical use in resource-limited IoT settings. The 
proposed DNN and Blockchain Technology (DNNs-BCT) framework mitigates these limitations by establishing 
a novel DL and blockchain integration wherein a lightweight DNN architecture enhances anomaly detection, 
and a smart contract-based blockchain mechanism guarantees secure, immutable logging and automated 
remediation. This approach improves threat intelligence, scalability, and real-time flexibility while decreasing 
computing complexity, representing a notable breakthrough over traditional methods.
Contribution 1: Hybrid AI-blockchain security framework
It presents a blockchain-based cybersecurity architecture and an integrated DNN for real-time anomaly 
identification and prevention in IoT networks.
In Fig.  1, combining anomaly detection driven by artificial intelligence with blockchain-based threat 
response ensures excellent security for IoT networks. IoT devices generate preprocessed traffic data meant to 
provide insightful analysis. A DNN model detects threats as either standard or aberrant while analyzing this 
processed data using adaptive learning and multi-layer feature extraction. The system generates notifications

resposta.resumo: O artigo propõe o framework DNNs‑BCT, que combina uma arquitetura DNN leve com contratos inteligentes em blockchain para detectar e prevenir anomalias em redes IoT. Aponta limitações de técnicas existentes, como altas taxas de falsos positivos e sobrecarga computacional, e descreve como a integração proposta melhora a integridade dos dados, reduz a latência e aumenta a escalabilidade, especialmente em ambientes de recursos limitados.
